title: every-device-has-a-presence
owner: CC (the build and proofs). Akien (the Murderbot frame, the process ladder, the bounce mechanism
intention: Every device has a PRESENCE — an always-on shim that answers what it is and how it is (never booted / running / offline-with-last-known), carries the four floor panes (status, settings, console, chat) and a declared verb set, and gives the same answers over the command line, the bus, and the web. Only the query processing belongs to the device itself.
why: Akien's own stated why, in his own words, about the embeddings generator echoing an embedding into its chat window: 'why the hell would anybody ever need that? Because then we can use it to prove to me it's working.' The chat window is the universal PROOF SURFACE — which is why it is FLOOR and not per-device, and why the useless-looking echo is the point rather than a feature request. A device you cannot address is a device you cannot check, and a fleet of thirteen you cannot check is a fleet you are trusting on narration (Law 3).
traces_to: Law 3 (nothing is known until measured — the chat window IS the measurement surface); Law 4 (presence carried by BaseShim is physics, presence each device remembers to implement is policy); Law 6 (the shim is the device's persistent front and process-manager — 'all of this is shim code stuff except the actual query processing' is an ownership ruling); Law 7 (never-booted and offline are loud honest answers; a silent nothing is the violation; a bounce rides a RECORD channel so it never collapses); Telos 2 (Cairn has a USER).

proves_green.prove_gate: the tester runs proofs with teeth: every device answers a presence query from CLI, bus, and web with the same content; a never-booted device answers without being booted; a downed device answers offline with a stamped last-known; every page carries four floor panes with absent-with-reason; the chat window takes at least the verbs its CLI takes; no envelope carries a channel outside the four; and a bounce returns to sender and is readable in the sender's public feed. Built on the real roster, not mocks — the defects measured at cast (the invented chat channel, the two-pane floor, deliver waking a sleeping device) are the first teeth.
proves_green.entry_gate: BUILDME refuses without a berthed chart chain and intent berth (both on file).
proves_green.durability: committed and pushed to both repos.

falsifier.proves_red: DONE when, on the live roster: every device answers a presence query from all three faces (CLI, bus, web) with the same content; a never-booted device answers 'never booted' WITHOUT being booted by the asking; a downed device answers offline with a stamped last-known status; every device's page carries all four floor panes with an honest absent-with-reason wherever nothing stands behind one; the chat window takes at least the verbs its CLI takes; no envelope anywhere carries a channel outside the bus's four; and a message a shim cannot honestly hand to its device is returned to sender and READABLE IN THE SENDER'S PUBLIC FEED, with the trouble raised at the sender. Read from the instruments, never from narration. WRONG INTENT if presence goes green for a device with no process: BaseShim.running today means 'an object was constructed in this address space', and a health surface built on it reports healthy for a device that never ran — a green that means nothing is worse than the silence it replaces. ALSO WRONG INTENT if the bounce lane fills with troubles whose fixes all land at the receiver (the WATCHME's kill).
falsifier.horizon: The encapsulation pass (child 1) runs first by Akien's ruling. The shim work (BaseShim carrying four panes, verb set, presence answer) is composition of what already exists — the measurement at cast names what is genuinely absent. The process ladder (ground loop → bus+shims → devices) is the distant milestone.

children: the-encapsulation-pass — ADDED 2026-08-11 on Akien's question, and it runs FIRST because it is a PRECONDITION of the process ladder rather than a consequence of it. For each cross-device edge, read what actually crosses: which functions, whether state or a live connection rides along, whether the caller survives the callee restarting. Classify as legitimate composition / a call that must become a message / a layering inversion. The import graph is the map, not the finding. Three findings already stand as its seed (encapsulation_measured above). May warrant its own cast when /chart reaches it; carried here so it cannot be lost.

the-domains-become-devices — db_domain and inference_domain are modules, not devices, which is the single structural blocker to Akien's stated why ('restart almost any part of the system for update without restarting the whole thing'). UU had both proxies as bus devices; Cairn does not. Downstream of the encapsulation pass, because what crosses those edges is what determines whether the change is a wrapper or a rewrite.
how: Build BaseShim presence: always-on front that answers what-it-is and how-it-is (never-booted / running / offline-with-last-known), carries the device's declared panes, and manages the device process. Children decompose the contract, states, panes, console, chat, mail, CLI, and bus.

watchme.trigger: Every clear of a bounce-raised trouble — the event that already fires, since the clear demands a what_changed. The probe reads bounce-raised troubles cleared AFTER THIS NODE'S PROVED CROSSING (the era floor) and classifies each what_changed by WHERE the fix landed: at the SENDER or at the RECEIVER. Fires when the receiver-side share exceeds half over at least 8 clears, or when a bounce-raised trouble stands live past 14 days with the same sender still sending.
watchme.enough: CLEARED once >= 8 post-era bounce-raised troubles have been cleared AND >= 6 were fixed at the SENDER. The kill is equally informative and retires it too: a receiver-side majority says the trouble is raised on the innocent party, which is a spec change, not a tuning. The era floor is load-bearing (the lesson of watchme-emits-a-probe): without it the corpus is the bounces CC causes and clears inside this very build. Akien may retire the watch by ruling.
watchme.carrier: a verdict artifact against THIS ticket's falsifier, via cairn.machines.chart.verdict.write_verdict — naming the post-era cleared count, the sender/receiver split with each deciding what_changed quoted, and any bounce-raised trouble whose prior_attempts shows a renegotiation that did not hold
watchme.consumer: AKIEN, through the owner's gate. The premise under test is his, in his own words, so a measured 'the fixes all landed at the receiver' is a spec-changing input, not a detail. The probe deposits and pokes; it has NO authority to back-edge this node (Law 6).

chart_claim: none, because no chart chain was run — backfilled by ticket inspector 2026-08-26. BUILDME entry gate (buildme_rides_the_sorted) is where this is answered or the chain is run.
the_ruling_that_shaped_it: Akien, 2026-08-11: MURDERBOT. The pane set IS the channel set, projected — and this was already the bus's founding metaphor (cairn/devices/bus/bus.py:24-29, the charter's `entry`, CairnCommons/intentions-not-beside-code/I-heartbeat-probes-and-bus.md:201-205, the Murderbot-feeds model, Martha Wells). announce = the PUBLIC feed (a builder announces completion publicly, not every step — the steps are in INFO); personal = the PERSONAL feed (Akien and CC chatting); info + debug = the CONSOLE pane, selected by buttons across the top with INFO the default (the stdout equivalent). Settings carries a circuit breaker. Public feed is a CHAT CHANNEL as well as an announce space — 'you me and igor can all chat about something', 'you me and hex via the librarian can talk over in the librarian's public chat about some bug he finds in himself'. And bounces are visible there: a bounce is something in the public feed, with its bounce message.

the_process_ladder.ruled: Akien, 2026-08-11 — this CLOSES the open sequencing question this ticket was cast with.
the_process_ladder.the_story_that_gives_the_why: 'There was a time before the ground loop idea where you'd spun up dozens of processes, deamons everywhere. it was faster to reboot than try and close them all. that's why the ground loop exists.' The ground loop is not a scheduler. It is the one process you are allowed to leave running, and it exists as the answer to a system nobody could shut down.
the_ladder: process #1 — THE GROUND LOOP. 'everything else can be brought down and the ground loop can still provide the pulse to bring it back up.'

process #2 — THE BUS, THE SHIMS, and related things. NOTE THE CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS TICKET: shims are resident together in process 2, NOT one process per device. That is what makes presence work at all — the shim is always-on because it lives in a process that is always up, it can answer 'never booted' because no device process was ever spawned, and it can answer 'offline with last known' because it OUTLIVES the device it manages. CC's cast-time lean (build the process boundary for the librarian first as a proving ground) was solving a problem this layout does not have, and is withdrawn.
whys_in_his_words: 'this allows us to restart almost any part of the system for update without restarting the whole thing'
'a single component can crash hard, and the system can keep going'
'later, the system as a whole will respond to the resulting trouble ticket(s) for such an event without me' — the unattended-recovery aim, which is what the trouble lane is FOR
'process isolation for protection, for encpsulation. because that keeps everything as simple as possible.'
the_process_ladder.prior_art_he_named: In UU, the database proxy and the inference proxy were THEMSELVES BUS DEVICES. Measured in Cairn 2026-08-11: they are not. See encapsulation_measured below.

encapsulation_measured.asked_by: Akien, 2026-08-11: 'you might want to ASK YOURSELF if we should do a pass for encapsulation adherence and appropriate boundries given it's been running as a unit?' — CC's answer, measured rather than agreed with: YES, and it goes BEFORE the split, not after.
encapsulation_measured.finding_1_the_domains_are_not_devices: cairn/devices/db_domain/store.py and cairn/devices/inference_domain/domain.py declare NO Device or Shim class — they are MODULES, reached by direct function import. Every other thing on the roster subclasses BaseDevice; the two domains are the exception, and they are the two whose independent restartability Akien named as the point. Direct importers today (non-proof): bus/bus.py, librarian/trees.py, skill_block/counters.py and inference_domain/domain.py all take `from cairn.devices.db_domain import store`; librarian/live.py and intention_extractor/live.py take `from cairn.devices.inference_domain import domain, host`. So restarting the database proxy today means restarting everyone who imported it.
encapsulation_measured.finding_2_the_gate_is_at_the_wrong_layer: import_sieve DOES enforce that only db_domain touches 5432 and only inference_domain dials the inference host — the owner-gate is real (Law 6). But it is an IMPORT-NAMESPACE door: it can say 'reach the DB only through this module', it cannot say 'only through this PROCESS'. So encapsulation is enforced at exactly the layer the process split makes insufficient. This is the CLAUDE.md residue ('a subprocess dials and imports nothing, and a dynamic import is invisible') coming due, and the ladder is what makes it due.
encapsulation_measured.finding_3_the_base_reaches_up: cairn/tools/base/transitions.py — the emit chokepoint, inherited by EVERY device — imports FIVE other devices: build_inspector (x5), tester, orient, charter, chart. Four are deliberately lazy (function-local, commented 'keep import dependency-light'); line 122 is top-level (`from cairn.tools.charter import projector`). It is not accidental — the chokepoint must call the gates — but it means the layer UNDER every device reaches UP into five of them, which is the widest coupling in the system sitting at the bottom of it.
encapsulation_measured.the_refinement_that_makes_the_pass_hones: AN IMPORT IS A PROXY FOR COUPLING, NOT COUPLING ITSELF. A module that imports `store` and calls one pure function is differently coupled from one holding a connection across a call. Reading the import graph and calling it the finding would repeat exactly the mistake that killed the census on mail-arrives-and-what-cannot-marks-itself (CC proposed reading class structure; Akien: ask the running device). So the pass reads WHAT CROSSES EACH EDGE — which functions, whether state or a live connection rides along, whether the caller survives the callee restarting — with the import graph as the MAP, not the measurement.
encapsulation_measured.why_before_the_split_and_not_after: Akien's own story is the argument. Process isolation WITHOUT encapsulation adherence buys the worst of both: the daemon zoo that was faster to reboot than to shut down, now failing across a wire as well. If the boundaries do not hold, splitting into processes does not deliver 'restart one thing' or 'one component crashes and the system keeps going' — it delivers thirteen things that still cannot be restarted independently, plus IPC. The split's whole value IS the boundaries, so the boundaries are what must be measured first.

measured_at_cast.already_built: The chat pane RENDERS end to end (cairn/devices/web_server/render.py:147-172, transcript + form), the librarian DECLARES it (cairn/devices/librarian/trees.py:541-545), and a proof walks a POSTed utterance through the shim (proofs/test_web_server_chat.py). introspect() (cairn/tools/base/device.py:82) and active_page() (cairn/tools/base/shim.py:286) already give a floor-plus-declared-panes shape with ABSENT-WITH-REASON for an unwired pane — which is exactly the Scraps case (Akien's UU catch-all script device, given a chat window it could not honestly use, barking at anything that was not a slash command). bus.digest() already collapses a diagnostic channel to count+tail and REFUSES to collapse a record channel, which is the console pane's read arriving with its Law 7 tooth attached. This node is mostly COMPOSITION, not construction.
measured_at_cast.genuinely_absent: No pane kind 'console' exists anywhere in the tree. No shim spawns a process (no subprocess/Popen/fork). No verb set. No presence answer that works without waking the device. No CLI path to any device (bin/cairn dispatches to bin/cmd/<name> and there is no device fallback). The bus has no reply.
measured_at_cast.defects_found: (1) 'chat' is a channel that should never have existed, invented at TWO addresses — cairn/devices/web_server/render.py:165 hardcodes it in the form's hidden field, cairn/devices/librarian/trees.py:552 accepts only it — while the bus's falsifier reds on an unknown channel, so the one device with a real receive is structurally unreachable BECAUSE OF the invention. (2) The floor built at cairn/tools/base/shim.py:309-311 is two panes; it should be four. (3) BaseShim.deliver calls _ensure_device() BEFORE it checks for a receive, so it WAKES a device in order to discover the device cannot help — the sleep/wake model violated at the exact seam that exists to honour it. Found against code written 2026-08-10.

open_at_cast: CLOSED SAME DAY — THE PROCESS MODEL. Cast open ('sequencing, so Akien's, asked twice and not yet answered'); ruled hours later. See the_process_ladder above: ground loop is process #1, the bus + shims + related are process #2, each device is its own process. CC's lean (build the boundary for the librarian first as a proving ground) is WITHDRAWN — shims being resident together in process 2 is what makes an always-on shim cheap, and it removes the problem that lean was solving. What remains open beneath it is the encapsulation pass, now a child.
